Nature of Roots of a Quadratic Equation

For a general equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **Discriminant** (D = b² − 4ac) determines the type of roots.

Real and Distinct Roots

If D > 0, the equation has two **distinct real roots**.

Real and Equal Roots

If D = 0, the equation has two **equal real roots** (also called a perfect square trinomial).

No Real Roots

If D < 0, the equation has **no real roots**; instead, it has complex or imaginary roots.</p
